ing: 4 thin cutlets, or pork loin cutlets
st: Pound the cutlets between plastic wrap to about 1/4 inch thick, then pat dry and season both sides with the salt.
Set up three shallow dishes: the flour in one, the eggs beaten with the milk in the second, and the breadcrumbs in the third.
Coat each cutlet in flour and shake off the extra. Dip in egg, then lay it on the breadcrumbs and press lightly. Do not press hard; the crumbs should stay loose.
Heat the oil and butter together in a wide skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers, about 340°F (170°C).
Fry one or two cutlets at a time. Swirl the pan gently so hot fat washes over the top and puffs the coating.
Cook about 2 minutes per side until deep golden. Pork must reach 145°F (63°C).
Lift the schnitzels out and drain on paper towels. Serve at once with lemon wedges.
Put the beef and bones in a large pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil and skim off the gray foam that rises.
Heat a dry skillet and char the cut sides of the onion for 3 minutes. Add to the pot with the peppercorns, bay leaves, and salt.
Lower the heat so the water barely bubbles. Cover partly and simmer for 2 hours 30 minutes, until the beef is very tender.
Add the carrots and celery and simmer 25 more minutes until soft.
While it cooks, stir the grated horseradish and the grated apples together to make the sauce. Add a pinch of salt.
Lift out the beef and let it rest for [[10 minutes]]. Strain the broth and keep it hot.
Slice the beef across the grain. Serve with the carrots, a ladle of broth, and the apple horseradish. Sprinkle with chives.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onions and cook, stirring often, for 20 minutes until deeply soft and golden. Do not rush this step.
Add the garlic and caraway and cook for 1 minute.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika right away so it does not burn and turn bitter.
Stir in the tomato paste, then add the beef cubes, salt, and pepper. Mix until the meat is coated.
Return to medium heat and add the broth and vinegar. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook on low for 2 hours, stirring now and then, until the beef is fork tender. Add a little water if it looks dry.
Taste and adjust the salt. Serve in bowls with bread, noodles, or boiled potatoes.

ing: divided, plus more for the water
st: Whisk the flour, [[1 tsp]] of the salt, and the nutmeg together in a bowl. Beat in the eggs and milk until you have a thick, smooth, sticky batter. Rest it for [[15 minutes]].
Melt [[2 tbsp]] of the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onions for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until deep golden brown. Set aside.
Bring a big pot of water to a boil and salt it well.
Press the batter through a spaetzle maker or a large-holed colander directly into the boiling water, working in batches.
When the noodles float to the top, cook 1 more minute, then lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). In a baking dish, layer the hot noodles with the cheese, starting and ending with cheese. Add the remaining butter in small pieces.
Bake for 8 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Top with the browned onions, pepper, and chives. Serve immediately.
Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, and salt until you have a smooth thin batter with no lumps. Let it rest for [[15 minutes]].
Melt a little of the butter in a nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Pour in a thin layer of batter, tilting the pan so it spreads. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the underside is golden and the top is set.
Flip and cook the other side for 1 minute. Slide it out onto a board. Repeat with the rest of the batter to make about 4 pancakes.
Let the pancakes cool a few minutes, then roll each one up and slice it into thin ribbons.
Heat the beef stock in a pot until steaming hot. Taste and add salt if needed.
Divide the pancake strips among bowls, ladle the hot stock over them, and sprinkle with chives.
Put the bread cubes in a large bowl.
Melt the butter in a small pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft and glassy, then stir in half the parsley.
Beat the eggs with the warm milk, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Pour the egg mixture and the onion over the bread. Add the flour and mix gently with your hands. Let it stand for [[20 minutes]] so the bread soaks up the liquid.
With wet hands, shape the mixture into 8 firm balls the size of a tennis ball. If they crack, add a splash of milk.
Bring a wide pot of salted water to a gentle boil. Lower the dumplings in and reduce the heat to a low simmer.
Cook uncovered for 20 minutes, turning once, until they are puffed and firm.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and sprinkle with the remaining parsley. Serve with roasts or goulash.
Whisk the flour, milk, egg yolks, [[1 tbsp]] sugar, vanilla, and salt into a smooth batter. Stir in the raisins.
In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites until foamy, then add [[2 tbsp]] sugar and beat until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold the whites into the batter with a spatula, keeping as much air as you can.
Melt [[1 tbsp]] of the butter in a large ovenproof skillet over medium heat. Pour in all the batter.
Cook for 4 minutes until the bottom is golden. Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) while you wait.
Cut the pancake into quarters and flip each piece. Bake for 5 minutes to cook the top through.
Using two forks, tear the pancake into rough bite-sized pieces. Add the remaining butter and toss over medium heat for 2 minutes until lightly caramelized.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve hot, ideally with stewed plums or applesauce.
Mix the flour, water, oil, and salt into a soft dough. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth, then coat with a little oil and rest it covered for [[30 minutes]].
Toss the apple slices with the sugar, cinnamon, and raisins in a bowl.
Toast the breadcrumbs in [[2 tbsp]] of the butter in a pan for 3 minutes until golden.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). On a floured cloth, roll the dough out, then stretch it with the backs of your hands until paper thin and about 18 by 24 inches.
Brush the dough with [[2 tbsp]] of the melted butter and scatter the toasted crumbs over the bottom third.
Spread the apple mixture on top of the crumbs. Fold in the short sides, then roll up the strudel using the cloth to help.
Move the strudel seam side down onto a lined baking sheet, curving it to fit. Brush the top with the remaining butter.
Bake for 40 minutes until deep golden brown. Cool for 15 minutes, dust with powdered sugar, and slice.

ing: softened, plus extra for the pan
st: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9-inch springform pan and line the bottom with parchment.
Melt [[3 oz]] of the chocolate gently in a bowl over a pot of simmering water, then let it cool until lukewarm.
Beat the butter and powdered sugar together for 4 minutes until pale and fluffy. Beat in the egg yolks one at a time, then the melted chocolate and vanilla.
In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites with the salt until foamy, then slowly add the sugar and beat to stiff peaks.
Fold a third of the whites into the chocolate mixture, then fold in the flour and the rest of the whites gently.
Pour the batter into the pan and bake for 50 minutes, until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs.
Cool the cake in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out on a rack and cool completely. Slice it in half horizontally.
Spread half of the jam between the layers. Brush the remaining jam over the top and sides.
Heat the cream until steaming, pour over [[2 oz]] of chopped chocolate with the corn syrup, and stir until smooth. Cool until slightly thick.
Pour the glaze over the cake and smooth it with a spatula. Let it set for [[1 hour]] before slicing.
Boil the whole unpeeled potatoes in water for 25 minutes until tender. Drain, peel while warm, and mash or press through a ricer. Cool for 15 minutes.
Mix the potatoes with the flour, egg, and salt. Knead briefly into a soft dough; add a spoonful more flour only if very sticky.
Cut the apricots along one side and take out the pit. Put a sugar cube in each cavity.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces. Flatten each in your hand, set an apricot in the middle, and wrap the dough around it. Roll into a smooth ball.
Bring a wide pot of salted water to a gentle simmer. Add the dumplings and cook for 12 minutes; they will float when done.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a skillet and toast the breadcrumbs with the [[3 tbsp]] sugar for 4 minutes until golden.
Lift the dumplings out with a slotted spoon and roll them in the buttered crumbs.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve warm.

ing: such as salami or Kabanos, sliced
st: Take the cheese, ham, and sausage out of the fridge [[15 minutes]] before serving so the flavors open up.
Slice the sausage and cheese into thin rounds. Fold or roll the ham slices.
Slice the bread and spread a thin layer of butter on each slice.
Wash and slice the radishes and the pickles.
Arrange the ham, sausage, and cheese in groups on a wooden board.
Place the pickles, radishes, and bread beside the meat and cheese.
Put the grated horseradish in a small bowl on the board and sprinkle the butter and radishes with chives.
